area: 2D segmentation architectures for PC12 cell body + neurite (thin tubular) segmentation at n≈70 labeled images (phase-contrast + fluorescence), with open-source runnable candidates, topology-aware options, nnU-Net v2 state, small-data best practice, and 2024–25 neurite/PC12 literature

candidates.name: U-Net (plain, 2015)
candidates.what_it_does: Contracting-expanding CNN with dense skip connections; the biomedical segmentation workhorse. The original paper was built precisely for the small-data regime: trained end-to-end from very few images (~40 annotated) with heavy augmentation, and it won the 2015 ISBI cell-tracking challenge on transmitted-light (phase contrast + DIC) images — the same modality as your PC12 data.
candidates.pc12_fit: Direct precedent: original paper's cell-tracking track was phase-contrast/DIC cell images. At n≈70, plain U-Net with nnU-Net-style augmentation is the lowest-risk, best-evidenced choice. Export to ONNX is trivial and mature.
candidates.neurite_support: Partial. Pixel-wise so it can learn thin structures, but vanilla Dice/CCE losses do not enforce connectivity — you must add clDice/Tversky (see techniques) to avoid broken/fragmented neurites and false blobs.
candidates.small_data_fit: Best-in-class: architecture was explicitly designed for ~40 images + augmentation. The anchor point for all small-data evidence in this survey.
candidates.notes: GPL-3.0 of Pytorch-UNet is fine for a course project; if the final desktop app will be distributed, prefer the Apache-2.0 MONAI/nnU-Net implementation to avoid copyleft concerns (verify with your department's policy).

candidates.name: UNet++ (nested U-Net, 2018)
candidates.what_it_does: Deeply supervised encoder-decoder with nested dense skip pathways that close the semantic gap between encoder/decoder feature maps; +3.9 IoU avg over U-Net on medical datasets incl. nuclei segmentation in microscopy (paper abstract, verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Strong candidate: deep supervision is a natural regularizer at n≈70 (multi-level loss = more gradient signal per image), and it was evaluated on nuclei-scale microscopy structures.
candidates.neurite_support: Partial — same story as U-Net; pair with clDice/Tversky for the neurite branch. Nested skips help boundary fidelity for thin structures, but no topology guarantee.
candidates.license: Official repo: ASU non-commercial research license (verified by reading LICENSE); MIT via segmentation_models.pytorch / keras-unet-collection (both verified)
candidates.small_data_fit: Good — deep supervision + nested dense connections are known to help small-data biomedical tasks; evaluated on small-structure microscopy (nuclei).
candidates.notes: Use the MIT-licensed segmentation_models.pytorch 'unetplusplus' for the final deliverable (the official repo is non-commercial-only). Paper: arXiv:1807.10165 (verified).

candidates.name: UNet3+ (2021)
candidates.what_it_does: U-Net variant that re-thinks the full-resolution path: all intermediate skip features are upsampled back to full resolution and concatenated, preserving 1-pixel boundary detail that classic U-Net downsample/upsample loses. Targeted at small/thin-structure segmentation (polyps, nuclei).
candidates.pc12_fit: One of the best architectural matches for thin 1–2 px neurites in 2D: the full-resolution path explicitly preserves fine tubular detail. At n≈70 it is comparable in parameter count to U-Net, so no extra data hunger.
candidates.neurite_support: Good (architecturally): full-res skips keep single-pixel strands intact; still needs clDice/Tversky for guaranteed connectivity.
candidates.code: https://github.com/qubvel-org/segmentation_models.pytorch (model 'unet3plus', MIT, verified in repo); alternative: https://github.com/avBuffer/UNet3plus_pth (no license file, verified)
candidates.small_data_fit: Good — same parameter budget as U-Net; the win is in boundary fidelity, which is exactly the neurite failure mode.
candidates.notes: Official paper ('UNet3+: Re-thinking full-resolution path for image segmentation', Computers in Biology and Medicine, 2021) could not be re-verified via DOI in this session — mark paper as unverified if you cite it; the repo/architecture is solid. The claimed official repo zcasky/UNet3Plus returns 404 (checked).

candidates.name: nnU-Net v2 (ResEnc presets, 2024–2025 state)
candidates.what_it_does: Self-configuring segmentation framework: dataset fingerprint → preprocessing, normalization, patch size, batch size, network topology, augmentation, 5-fold splits, model selection and postprocessing — all automated. v2 adds hierarchical labels, unified trainer, native multi-GPU DDP, cross-platform support. 2024 'ResEnc' presets add ResNet/ConvNeXt-style residual encoders: nnUNetResEncUNetM (~9 GB VRAM), L (~23 GB, recommended default), XL (~37 GB) (official resenc_presets.md table, verified). Supports supervised pretraining/finetuning (-pretrained_weights) and finetuning from nnssl self-supervised checkpoints (docs verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Excellent as a baseline and as the mainline trainer for the cell-body class: automates exactly the 5-fold-by-image protocol the team planned, handles 2D natively, and ResEnc L fits the A5000 24 GB. At n≈70 the self-configured aggressive data augmentation is the main reason to use it over a hand-rolled loop.
candidates.neurite_support: No — default loss is Dice+CE; no clDice, no topology awareness. You must subclass nnUNetTrainer (supported, documented) to add clDice/Tversky for the neurite class, or run the neurite head in a separate custom loop.
candidates.compute: Standard 2D config: well under 10 GB; ResEnc L: ~23 GB (3D table; 2D less) → A5000 OK; ResEnc XL: ~37 GB → use the A6000 48 GB
candidates.small_data_fit: Strong: designed for exactly 10s–1000s of labeled samples; augmentation + 5-fold + postprocessing auto-tuned from the data itself. Known caveat from the 2024 'nnU-Net Revisited' paper (arXiv:2404.09556, verified): validate carefully — small datasets amplify overfitting to fold-split artifacts, so keep your planned split-by-image CV and report per-fold variance.
candidates.effort: ~1 week to pipeline; then unattended overnight runs
candidates.notes: Known failure modes at small n: (1) fingerprint-driven patch/batch choices can be suboptimal when the dataset is tiny — inspect the generated plans JSON and hand-edit if needed (plans are editable, documented); (2) it cannot learn connectivity for tubular structures (no clDice by default); (3) cascade configs are skipped for 2D-only data (fine). VRAM table and ResEnc L recommendation are from the official repo docs (checked).

candidates.name: clDice / soft-clDice loss (Shit et al., CVPR 2021)
candidates.what_it_does: Connectivity-preserving loss computed on the intersection of masks and their morphological skeletons; the paper proves clDice guarantees topology preservation up to homotopy equivalence for binary 2D/3D segmentation, and the differentiable soft-clDice loss improves connectivity, graph similarity and volumetric scores on five datasets including vessels, roads AND NEURONS (2D and 3D) (abstract verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: This is the single most important technique for the neurite class: it directly optimizes what your metrics (clDice, Betti error) measure, and the paper's benchmark set explicitly includes neuron data — the closest domain to PC12 neurites.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — designed and validated for tubular structures incl. neurons, not just vessels. Most 'topology-aware' published work on real cells uses this loss.
candidates.code: https://github.com/jocpae/clDice (official, MIT, verified; PyTorch+TF); also https://github.com/dmitrysarov/clDice (PyTorch, no license) and https://github.com/jacobkoenig/clDice-Loss (Keras)
candidates.compute: Loss only; negligible overhead (skeletonization per batch)
candidates.small_data_fit: Essential at n≈70: acts as a structural prior that substitutes for data — the network gets per-iteration topological feedback instead of pure pixel statistics.
candidates.notes: Combine as weighted sum (e.g., 0.5·Dice + 0.5·soft-clDice, or Dice+Tversky+clDice) — soft-clDice alone can be noisy in early training when predictions are sparse. The official repo is small (loss module); drop-in PyTorch. The paper is arXiv:2003.07311v7 (verified).

candidates.name: SA-UNet (Spatial Attention U-Net, 2020)
candidates.what_it_does: Lightweight U-Net with a spatial-attention gate and structured dropout convolution blocks, explicitly built so it 'does not require thousands of annotated training samples'; SOTA on DRIVE (40 training images) and CHASE_DB1 (60) retinal vessel benchmarks (abstract verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Good thin-structure template: retinal vessels are the standard proxy problem for neurites in 2D, and this paper is one of the few vessel-specialist architectures with explicit small-data evidence (40–60 images) plus overfitting control (structured dropout) that transfers to n≈70.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes (by design for thin tubular structures); connectivity still needs a clDice-style loss to be guaranteed.
candidates.code: https://github.com/changluguo/SA-UNet (author repo; URL not re-verified in this session — verify before citing)
candidates.license: Unverified (repo not opened in this session)
candidates.small_data_fit: Explicit: paper's stated premise is few-hundred-to-tens of annotated images with augmentation + structured dropout.
candidates.notes: Use as the 'vessel-transfer' ablation arm: retrain SA-UNet on PC12 neurites with clDice. If it beats plain U-Net on thin-structure recall, it's a clean thesis result on domain transfer (retina→neurons).

candidates.name: DR-VNet (Dense Residual U-Net, 2021)
candidates.what_it_does: Combines residual dense blocks with squeeze-and-excitation residual blocks to recover thin/tiny vessels; validated on three retinal datasets with sensitivity gains specifically on small vessels (abstract verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Solid thin-structure specialist for the neurite head; SENet blocks give channel recalibration that helps when neurites are a tiny fraction of pixels.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — optimized for sensitivity on the thinnest tubular structures (the same failure mode as faint PC12 neurites in phase contrast).
candidates.code: Paper: arXiv:2111.04739 (verified). Official code: not found/verified in this session.
candidates.small_data_fit: Good — built on the same few-hundred-image retinal benchmark culture (DRIVE/CHASE/STARE).
candidates.notes: Same role as SA-UNet: domain-transfer ablation. If only one vessel-specialist arm fits in 15 weeks, pick SA-UNet (verified paper + attention mechanism is easier to justify to a reviewer).

candidates.name: TransUNet (2021)
candidates.what_it_does: CNN encoder → tokenized features → Transformer (global self-attention) → U-Net decoder with high-res skip features. Strong long-range context modeling for medical segmentation (abstract verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Weakest fit of the transformer options for n≈70: the transformer encoder is the most data-hungry component, and the 2024 'nnU-Net Revisited' benchmark (arXiv:2404.09556, verified) found CNN U-Net variants consistently outperform transformer models (SwinUNETR, nnFormer) even with 100–1000+ samples — the gap only grows when data shrinks. The 48 GB A6000 can afford the FLOPs, but extra VRAM does not substitute for 10× the labeled data.
candidates.neurite_support: Partial — global attention may help keep long neurite context, but no topology guarantee; still needs clDice.
candidates.compute: ~10 GB class at 512×512 2D (single-GPU design; fits 24 GB) — typical, not re-measured in this session
candidates.small_data_fit: Poor-to-fair: no small-data evidence in the paper (trained on large abdominal/cardiac datasets); transformer inductive bias needs data to beat plain CNNs.
candidates.notes: Worth running as ONE ablation row (it's cheap with nnU-Net-style automation and you have compute) to show 'transformer encoder does not help at n≈70' — that's a defensible negative result for the thesis. Do not make it the mainline.

candidates.name: Swin-UNet (ECCV Workshops 2022)
candidates.what_it_does: Pure hierarchical Swin-Transformer U-Net with shifted windows; competitive on abdominal/ACDC datasets.
candidates.pc12_fit: Same small-data objection as TransUNet, plus practical issues: the official repo has NO license file (verified via GitHub API), and 2024 benchmarking (nnU-Net Revisited, arXiv:2404.09556) shows transformer UNets losing to CNN UNets including residual-encoder CNNs.
candidates.neurite_support: Partial — windowed attention sees local context; no topology mechanism.
candidates.license: None (no LICENSE in repo, verified) — reimplementation required for a distributable app
candidates.small_data_fit: Poor: no small-data evidence; data-hungry hierarchical transformer.
candidates.notes: Skip for the mainline. If a reviewer asks for a Swin comparison, one overnight 5-fold run on the A6000 from a clean-room reimplementation suffices; do not build the final app on unlicensed code.

candidates.name: Attention U-Net (2018)
candidates.what_it_does: U-Net with attention gates that learn to suppress irrelevant regions while highlighting salient structures; minimal overhead, improves sensitivity across training sizes (abstract verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Moderate: attention gates help focus on cells/neurites against busy phase-contrast backgrounds (other cells, debris), but the paper's evidence is CT abdomen, not microscopy or tubular structures. At n≈70 the extra gate parameters are mild data hunger.
candidates.neurite_support: Partial — helps sensitivity, says nothing about connectivity.
candidates.code: https://github.com/LeeJunHyun/Image_Segmentation (PyTorch, no license, verified in search results); also in https://github.com/yingkaisha/keras-unet-collection (MIT, verified)
candidates.small_data_fit: Fair — attention helps small-data generalization somewhat, but no explicit small-data study.
candidates.effort: 1 week (drop-in via keras-unet-collection or SMP-style reimplementation)
candidates.notes: Candidate upgrade of the cell-body head if background clutter hurts recall in week-4 evaluation. Not a neurite solution by itself.

candidates.name: SegResNet (2018)
candidates.what_it_does: 3D MRI segmentation network with autoencoder (latent bottleneck) regularization of skip connections, reducing overfitting; baseline from the BrainLes 2018 workshop (reference verified in nnU-Net official docs).
candidates.pc12_fit: The autoencoder regularization is a legitimate small-data device, but the design is 3D-oriented; in 2D it reduces to a regularized U-Net with no edge over UNet++ at equal parameter budget.
candidates.code: In https://github.com/Project-MONAI/MONAI (Apache-2.0, reference verified via nnU-Net docs; MONAI repo not opened this session)
candidates.small_data_fit: Fair — regularization helps, but no thin-structure specialization and weaker evidence than UNet++ for your regime.
candidates.notes: Keep as a secondary baseline if you want to show regularization beats plain U-Net at n≈70; low priority otherwise.

candidates.name: FPN / FPUNet (feature pyramid decoder)
candidates.what_it_does: Multi-scale top-down feature pyramid with lateral connections (object-detection origin, arXiv:1612.03144 verified); as a segmentation decoder (FPUNet) it fuses multi-resolution features for pixel prediction.
candidates.pc12_fit: Decent general decoder (multi-scale helps when cell bodies vary in size), but for thin neurites the top-down upsampled path is exactly where 1-px detail is destroyed — opposite of what you want. Use it for the cell-body head only, if at all.
candidates.neurite_support: Poor — pyramid upsmoothing is the classic cause of broken thin strands.
candidates.notes: Not a differentiator for this task; UNet3+ is strictly better for thin structures at the same cost. Listed so it can be explicitly ruled out in the proposal.

candidates.name: DS-UNet (dual-stream U-Net, IEEE Access 2021)
candidates.what_it_does: Image-feature-fusion dual-stream U-Net benchmarked on retinal vessel segmentation (image stream + feature stream with parallel multi-scale convolutions).
candidates.pc12_fit: Conceptually fine (multi-scale dual stream for thin vessels), but the original repo could not be verified: GitHub search returned only a 2024 third-party clone without a license (GuanLi0818/DSUNet, 0 stars, no license, verified in search results).
candidates.code: Not verifiable: https://github.com/GuanLi0818/DSUNet (third-party, no license, created 2024) — treat as unofficial
candidates.small_data_fit: Unverified (original paper's datasets are standard retinal, ~40–2000 images).
candidates.notes: Skip unless you can verify the original IEEE Access 2021 paper and official code (not found in arXiv/Crossref/GitHub in this session). SA-UNet covers the same niche with verifiable assets.

candidates.name: VesselMUNet (U-Net + multi-head attention, vessel segmentation)
candidates.what_it_does: Reported in the field as a retinal-vessel U-Net enhanced with a multi-head attention module. IMPORTANT: could NOT be verified in this session — github.com/JianpengZhang/VesselMUNet returns 404 (user jianpengzhang exists but has no such repo, user repo list checked), GitHub code search for 'VesselMUNet' returns 0 results, arXiv full-text search returns 0, Crossref title search returns 0.
candidates.pc12_fit: Unverifiable — do not build the plan on it.
candidates.code: None found (verified absence, not absence of effort)
candidates.notes: Flag to the team: the commonly cited 'VesselMUNet' reference appears broken/untraceable in the public record as of this check. Replace with SA-UNet or DR-VNet (both verified). If you have the PDF of the paper, verify its exact venue/DOI before citing it in the thesis.

candidates.name: TransNewSeg (transformer retinal vessel segmentation)
candidates.what_it_does: Reported as a U-shaped transformer for retinal vessel segmentation. Like VesselMUNet, it could NOT be verified here: GitHub code search 'TransNewSeg' = 0 results, arXiv = 0, Crossref title search = 0.
candidates.small_data_fit: Unknown (transformers at n≈70 are the worst case anyway)
candidates.notes: Same treatment as VesselMUNet: verify the primary source (likely an IEEE Access 2024 paper) before citing; do not plan around it. If it exists, its transformer design carries the same small-data caveat as TransUNet.

candidates.name: MM-UNet (Morph Mamba U-Net, 2025)
candidates.what_it_does: 2025 retinal vessel segmentation network using Mamba (state-space) blocks for morphologically-aware thin-vessel modeling (repo description verified).
candidates.pc12_fit: Interesting 2025 SOTA for thin tubular structures, but: Mamba ONNX export for a desktop app is the weak link (operator support is still maturing), and it's a 2025 paper with a young codebase to adopt into a 15-week course project.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — designed for thin vessels with topology in mind.
candidates.compute: ~8–16 GB (typical SSM 2D net; not measured here)
candidates.notes: Keep as a literature-comparison point for 'thin-structure methods 2024–25'. Do not build the deliverable on Mamba: ONNX runtime support for ssm ops is the specific risk to the offline-desktop-app requirement.

candidates.name: MIX-Transformer (2021)
candidates.what_it_does: Multi-scale interleaved cross-attention transformer for medical segmentation (paper cited in the brief; not re-verified in this session — the arXiv IDs commonly associated with it could not be confirmed).
candidates.pc12_fit: Data-hungry transformer with, to the best of this session's verification, no official open-source code — a bad fit for a 2-person, 15-week, must-run-on-ONNX project.
candidates.notes: Drop from the shortlist; the verified transformer options (TransUNet as ablation) cover the 'we tried transformers' requirement.

candidates.name: Cellpose (for context)
candidates.what_it_does: StarDist-style amortized cell segmentation with style transfer; strong pretrained models for generic cell bodies across microscopes.
candidates.pc12_fit: Useful zero-shot/first-pass baseline on your 70 images (free labeled-prior), and a comparison row — but it is cell-BODY centric.
candidates.neurite_support: No — it does not segment neurites; do not count it toward the neurite pipeline.
candidates.code: https://github.com/musec-lab/cellpose (known from project brief; repo not re-opened this session)
candidates.small_data_fit: Excellent as a zero-shot baseline; fine-tuning possible but not needed at n≈70 for the comparison row.
candidates.notes: Run zero-shot Cellpose + StarDist in week 1 on a 10-image sample to calibrate how far the supervised pipeline must beat the off-the-shelf prior — that number anchors the thesis motivation.

bottom_line: For a 2-person, 15-week team with n≈70 images and 24+48 GB GPUs, the literature points to one clear mainline: a CNN U-Net family model (plain U-Net, UNet++, or UNet3+ — all ~same parameter budget, all runnable on the A5000, all ONNX-exportable) trained inside nnU-Net v2 for its free augmentation/5-fold/postprocessing automation, with a per-class multi-objective loss = Dice/Tversky for cell bodies + soft-clDice (jocpae/clDice, MIT) for neurites, since the clDice paper is the only topology-aware loss with proven guarantees AND a validated neuron benchmark. The 2024 'nnU-Net Revisited' evidence (arXiv:2404.09556) says transformers (TransUNet/Swin-UNet) lose to CNN U-Nets even at 100–1000 samples, so treat them as one ablation row, not the mainline; and note that the frequently-cited VesselMUNet and TransNewSeg repos could not be verified in the public record (404s/zero search hits) — do not build on them. The three highest-leverage differentiators that fit the budget: (1) semi-supervised pseudo-labeling on the unlabeled lab archive (the only realistic data-scaling lever), (2) making Betti-error/clDice-score the headline metric and demonstrating DSC≠topology, (3) a skeleton-graph morphometrics layer validated against expert-traced skeletons. Expected effort: weeks 1–3 baseline (Cellpose zero-shot + nnU-Net U-Net 5-fold), weeks 4–9 mainline with clDice + semi-supervision, weeks 10–15 graph validation, ONNX export, and XAI — comfortably within 15 weeks on the stated hardware.
